data.description:
Atin, 2026-10-02 (after the C11-257 run): live proofs that need real agents run in an Atlas sandbox guest, not on Hyperion. In C11-257 every live proof (Claude, Codex and Grok tabs receiving mail while waiting and busy) ran in tagged builds on Hyperion. The screen locked twice and stalled them (ghostty cannot create surfaces under a locked screen), tagged apps came to the front once, and the builds loaded the laptop. The C11-244 sandbox (`scripts/sandbox-up.sh`, a headless Tart macOS guest on Atlas) already runs a tagged c11 for clicks, screenshots and tests_v2; it does not yet run logged-in agents.

Goal: an orchestrator or lane owner can launch Claude Code, Codex and Grok agent tabs inside a sandbox guest's c11, drive them through the guest's c11 CLI over SSH, and read their screens, with nothing launched on Hyperion.

Scope:
1. Confirm the guest presents an unlocked Aqua session where c11 creates terminal surfaces (the C11-244 phase 2 probe), if not already recorded.
2. Agent CLIs in the guest: `claude`, `codex`, `grok` installed in the golden image (pinned versions recorded), or installed per clone if the image should stay minimal.
3. Credentials, never baked into the golden image: injected into each clone at `sandbox-up` from a mode-600 store on Atlas and destroyed with the clone. Decision for Atin before building: which identities. Our default is org-owned service identities over personal logins (Stage11 CLAUDE.md); list what each harness accepts headlessly (Claude long-lived token, Codex auth file or API key, Grok API key) and the cost of each.
4. A script, e.g. `scripts/sandbox-agent.sh <run-id> <kind> <brief-file>`, that launches an agent tab in the guest's c11 with the brief delivered as a file pointer, plus a read-screen helper. No focus or activation on the host.
5. Proof: rerun C11-257 sign-off steps 3-8 inside one guest (mail to a waiting and a busy Claude, Codex and Grok; the operator-draft step through the c11 seam), with Hyperion idle throughout.
6. Teach it: c11-hotload / c11-computer-use skills and the orchestrator delivery reference say live agent proofs run in the sandbox, with the command; sync installed skills.

Out of scope: a self-hosted GitHub runner (Atin, 2026-10-02: CI stays on GitHub-hosted runners).
data.title: Sandbox agents: run logged-in Claude, Codex and Grok tabs inside the Atlas sandbox for live proofs

data.body: Credentials decided (Atin, 2026-10-02): reuse the Overwatch box-seat credential path, no new logins. On Atlas, overwatch/launcher/kinds/{claude,codex,grok}.sh kind_credentials + launcher/agent-cred.py already export per-agent access credentials (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the per-account setup-token files, verified to bill the named account and picked by glideslope; CODEX_AUTH_JSON_B64 exported from the dedicated seat Codex login; a Grok access token exported from the dedicated seat Grok login), refreshed by seat.sh refresh. SEAT-MODEL.md section 11 is the policy. The sandbox stages the same secrets into each Tart clone the way prime-seat-image's entrypoint stages them into a box (0600 files, shims), and destroys them with the clone. If the exporters need a small refactor to be called from c11's sandbox scripts, make it in overwatch (fix upstream at the source).

Routing (Orchestrator, at intake): hard ticket (harness and credentials). Owner Opus high (Codex weekly quota was at 4%, so Astra moved off the owner seat), Review 1 Astra xhigh, Review 2 Grok. Atin approved starting the ticket 2026-10-02.

plan: sandbox agents for live proofs (C11-322 owner)

**Invariant.** No secret persists in the golden image or outlives its clone, and nothing on the run touches Hyperion's screen or focus. Concretely: (a) secrets are exported on Atlas only and travel Atlas -> guest over SSH stdin, never argv, never a host file, never a log line; (b) inside the guest they live only in the clone's disk (0600 files under a 0700 dir) and the clone is deleted at teardown; (c) the golden image is never booted or written by any sandbox script (the existing `refuse_protected` guard, and staging only ever targets `c11-sb-*`); (d) every command that touches an app or a screen runs inside the guest over SSH; Hyperion only runs ssh.

**Credentials (overwatch, one small commit on Forgejo main).** Add `seat.sh export-cred --agent claude|codex|grok [--account <call-sign>] [--min-hours H]`: loads the kind file and runs its existing `kind_credentials` (Claude token file + `claude-account whose` billing check, `agent-cred.py codex-export`, `agent-cred.py grok-export`), then prints one JSON object on stdout `{agent, account, expires_at, env:{NAME:value}}` built from `KIND_SECRET_ARGS`. No behavior change to `create`. Reason: c11's scripts need the same exporters outside a Prime box, and `kind_credentials` is only reachable from inside seat.sh today. Atlas's overwatch checkout is updated by `git pull`.

**Scripts (c11).**
- `scripts/sandbox-up.sh <run-id> <app> --agents claude,codex,grok`: after the app is live, stages agents; a staging failure is a failed up (clone torn down), the error names the kind and the fix.
- `scripts/sandbox-agent.sh <run-id> stage [kinds]`: copies Atlas's installed agent binaries into the clone (claude 2.1.287, codex 0.159.3, grok 1.0.46 today; versions recorded in run meta), installs them on the guest login PATH (`/usr/local/bin`), then pipes the exported credentials on stdin to a guest stager that writes: Claude token to `~/.c11-sandbox-secrets/claude-oauth` read by a `claude` shim that exports `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (Claude has no file login on macOS); Codex access-only `~/.codex/auth.json` (no refresh token); Grok access token to `~/.c11-sandbox-secrets/grok-token` served by a `grok-auth` external auth provider. First-run state seeded like prime-seat-image's entrypoint (Claude onboarding/trust/bypass, Codex trusted dir/no update check, Grok always-approve/telemetry off). Re-running `stage` refreshes (Grok tokens live 6 h).
- `scripts/sandbox-agent.sh <run-id> launch <kind> <brief-file> [--title T] [--model M]`: copies the brief into the guest and runs the guest's `c11 launch-agent --type <claude-code|codex|grok> --prompt-file <guest brief> --cwd ~/c11-sandbox/work --title T --json`, so the brief arrives as a file pointer; sets `mailbox.address`=title and `mailbox.delivery=stdin`; prints the guest tab and workspace refs.
- `scripts/sandbox-agent.sh <run-id> screen <tab> [--lines N]`: guest `c11 read-screen`. `scripts/sandbox-agent.sh <run-id> c11 <args...>`: any guest c11 CLI call against the guest socket (mailbox send, send --raw --no-submit, send-key, tree).
- `scripts/sandbox-agent.sh <run-id> wipe`: removes staged secrets in the guest; `sandbox-down.sh` calls it before `tart stop`/`tart delete` (belt; the delete is the guarantee).
- `scripts/sandbox-agent.sh <run-id> verify-clean`: after down, checks the clone is gone from `tart list` and `~/.tart/vms`, and greps the golden `disk.img` and the run's host dirs for the currently exported secret values (patterns fed through a file descriptor, background IO priority, only counts printed).

**Proof (one guest on Atlas, Hyperion idle).** Tagged build from this branch via `remote-build.sh`; `sandbox-up --agents claude,codex,grok`; launch `lc-claude`, `lc-codex`, `lc-grok` with a "reply with one word" brief; C11-257 sign-off steps 3-8 over `sandbox-agent.sh c11`: waiting push and busy (`sleep 20`) delivery per kind with mailbox events showing via push/drain exactly once, step 7 awkward title + `recv --drain`, step 8 operator draft placed with `send --raw --no-submit "hello wor"` (the debug seam the mailbox gate treats as a draft), mail buffered, then Return, draft turn first, mail as its own turn. Screens captured with `screen` and a `sandbox-shot`. Then `sandbox-down`, `verify-clean`. Teach: c11-hotload, c11-computer-use, orchestrator delivery reference (overwatch) say live agent proofs run in the sandbox with the commands; skill sync left to merge.

Current blocker to the proof only: both Atlas guest slots are held by other runs (c11-249-ui, c11-323-perf). Building meanwhile.

Orchestrator ruling on the Grok proof DECISION: option (1). Prove Claude and Codex mail steps 3-8 now; Grok counts as login proof (authenticated in the guest, reached xAI, refused only for weekly quota). Grok mail behavior itself was proven live in C11-257. Grok steps 3/4/6 in the sandbox rerun after the seat login's weekly reset (Tue 2026-10-06 10:31 PDT) and go on the hardening list; the PR does not wait for them. Claude steps run on Bravo (Alpha at 100%).

validation: C11-322 sandbox agents, proven in one Atlas guest (2026-10-02, 21:55-22:40 UTC)

**Setup.** Tagged app `c11 DEV c11-322` built on Atlas by `remote-build.sh` (base 92489ac3ad). The scripts ran on Atlas against the retained build with `C11_SANDBOX_HOST=local`, because the laptop-to-Atlas app upload stalled mid-stream; other lanes' rsyncs stalled the same way. Clone `c11-sb-c11-322-agents`: clone 1 s, boot 35 s. Hyperion ran only ssh: `pgrep -fl 'c11 DEV c11-322'` on Hyperion is empty, and no app was launched or focused there.

**Staging** (`sandbox-agent.sh <run> stage claude,codex,grok`). CLIs copied from Atlas: claude 2.1.287, codex-cli 0.159.3, grok 1.0.46. Credentials came from `seat.sh export-cred` (overwatch 39d90b8, Forgejo main): Claude billed Alpha, then Bravo (verified by `claude-account whose`), Codex used the seat login, Grok used the seat login. The guest got `~/.c11-sandbox-secrets/{claude-oauth,grok-token}` and `~/.codex/auth.json`, all `-rw-------` in a `drwx------` directory. No value was printed.

**Agents.** `sandbox-agent.sh <run> launch <kind> brief.md --title lc-<kind>`. All three started logged in, with no login prompt.
- Codex answered READY.
- Claude on Alpha reached the API and got "org's monthly spend limit" (Alpha weekly 100%). It was restaged on Bravo (`C11_SANDBOX_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT=bravo`) and answered READY.
- Grok reached xAI and got "You hit your weekly limit" (seat at 100% until Tue Oct 6). That is login-only proof, per Orchestrator option (1). Its mail steps rerun after the reset.

**C11-257 sign-off steps 3-8.** Mail was sent from a `sender` shell tab in the guest workspace. Delivery comes from the guest `c11 events` log; the turn order comes from each agent's own transcript.

| Step | Envelope | Events | Transcript order |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 Claude waiting | ...SNFV40 | accepted, inbox, **push** (1 s) | PONG-CL1 |
| 4 Claude busy (`sleep 20`) | ...VAJ3YB | handler `buffered` mid-turn, then **drain** at 22:03:30 | DONE-4, then Stop hook delivers the mail, then PONG-CL2 |
| 5 Codex waiting | ...MC2Z6Q | accepted, inbox, **push** (1 s) | PONG-CX1 |
| 5 Codex busy | ...KHRMYN | **push** at the idle edge 22:04:12 | DONE-5b (22:04:11), then the mail, then PONG-CX2 |
| 6 Grok | n/a | deferred: weekly limit | |
| 7 Awkward title (`a/b: c — … …`) | ...0RQZWZ | inbox, **drain** by `c11 mailbox recv --drain` in that tab | printed `hello-awkward` |
| 8 Operator draft | ...DB9DV6 | handler `buffered`; draft `❯ hello wor` intact 12 s later; **drain** at 22:04:58 | "hello world, answer … WORLD", then WORLD, then Stop hook delivers PONG-CL3 as its own turn, then PONG-CL3 |

Every envelope has exactly one non-inbox delivery. The draft was placed through the c11 seam (`send --raw --no-submit "hello wor"`), finished the same way, then `send-key enter`.

**Secrets gone, golden clean.**
- `sandbox-down`: `wiped=…/.c11-sandbox-secrets,…/.codex/auth.json`, then `deleted=c11-sb-c11-322-agents`.
- `verify-clean`: `clone=absent`, `clone_dir=absent`, `patterns=5 (self-test passed)` (two Claude accounts, Codex access and id tokens, Grok), `golden_disk_mtime=unchanged since stage`, `golden_disk=absent (bytes=32056427520)`, `host_sandbox_tree=absent`, `verify_clean=pass` (27 s).
- Positive control, a second clone `c11-322-ctl` brought up with `sandbox-up --agents claude,codex,grok`: `verify-clean --control` gave `control_clone_disk=found`, and guest `fdesetup status` reported `FileVault is Off`. So the scan does see guest files, and the golden "absent" carries weight. After `sandbox-down`, `verify-clean` passed again (`golden_disk=absent`, `host_sandbox_tree=absent`).
- Leak sweep on Atlas for every staged value: `~/.overwatch-v2/launcher.log`, the run's evidence directory, and `~/c11-builds/c11-322` matched nothing.

**Found on the way, not ours to change.** Atlas's Homebrew `codex` carries `com.apple.quarantine`, and executing it over SSH hangs at `_dyld_start` (Gatekeeper first launch). Stage never runs it; it reads the version from the cask's `codex-package.json`. A Codex seat or any SSH-launched codex on Atlas would hang the same way. Clearing it is Atin's call: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex/0.159.3/bin/codex`.

Evidence (Atlas): `~/c11-sandbox-runner/c11-322/evidence-proof.log`, `evidence/{claude,codex}-scrollback.txt`, `evidence/grok-screen.txt`, `evidence/verify-clean*.txt`, `evidence/control.txt`, `evidence/final-display.png`.

review r1 FAIL @ 97e8cc26c3

Invariants: (a) exported credentials must never persist in the golden image, a repo, logs, argv, the PR, or beyond their clone's lifetime, and must not be displayed; (b) the run must not launch, activate, or focus anything on Hyperion; (c) it must not disturb Atlas's other VMs/services or bypass build admission.

Reviewed the seven-file diff 9cd41788261e3a02f32d46e81dd0e5aba18cd96e..97e8cc26c30cc939da7b3e3c24253fed0d03677d and Overwatch 39d90b8b7f9dcfe245d531a26dc23ce0db5d1504, including its kind_credentials and agent-cred.py dependencies. The review checkout is detached and clean; PR #562 still has that exact head. Read the ticket's credential decision, plan, validation, and Grok quota ruling. The default host path stays on Atlas and app operations stay in the guest; I found no new build-admission bypass or direct operation on another VM/service.

All five findings below block Review 1 under its discovery rule. Normal-use final-gate ranking is stated separately.

1. [P1] Cancelled agent staging escapes sandbox-up's cleanup. scripts/sandbox-up.sh:351-355 (the remote boot cleanup is disarmed at :340); scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:433-435. The new stage runs after the remote boot script has exited successfully, with no EXIT/INT/HUP/TERM cleanup in the outer sandbox-up. Cancel or terminate the command during the guest credential write or subsequent record creation and the explicit `if ! stage` error handler is bypassed: the detached Tart clone keeps running with any credentials already written. This also consumes a VM slot until someone manually runs down. A read-only subprocess probe of the exact added stage/cleanup branch, with fake stage/down commands, reached staging and skipped teardown under both SIGINT and SIGTERM (exits -2 and -15). Keep ownership/cleanup armed through staging and report teardown failure rather than silently orphaning the run. Normal-use final gate: BLOCKING; ordinary cancellation leaves a running credential-bearing clone.

2. [P1] Rotated credentials can produce a false clean verdict. scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:673-680, :719-721. verify-clean re-exports current tokens, detects missing historical fingerprints, but only prints the mismatch and leaves `bad=0`. For example, after a run lasts more than three hours, the Grok exporter can refresh its six-hour token to meet its three-hour minimum; an older, still-valid staged token left in an output file is no longer a search pattern. The command can then say `verify_clean=pass` without examining that value. Restaging and the independent seat refresh loop also trigger this. A synthetic execution of the actual fingerprint branch reported one missing staged value with `bad=0` and exit 0. Fail closed when any staged fingerprint is unavailable; a current-token scan cannot certify all historical values. Normal-use final gate: BLOCKING; cleanup can certify surviving credentials as absent during routine rotation.

3. [P1] Scan errors are converted to successful absence. scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:117-120, :147-155 (consumed at :689-693). Any open/read PermissionError or I/O error is silently skipped; every SEEK_DATA error is treated as end-of-file, including errors other than ENXIO. os.walk also ignores traversal errors by default. A secret-bearing artifact that is unreadable, or an unreadable golden image, can therefore yield `absent bytes=0`, exit 0, and a passing cleanup gate. Read-only probes of the extracted scanner against this source file gave: readable positive control -> found/exit 1; synthetic PermissionError -> absent bytes=0/exit 0; synthetic SEEK_DATA EINVAL -> absent bytes=0/exit 0. Propagate inaccessible/read-failed paths, distinguish ENXIO from unsupported/error seeks, and fail or use a valid full-read fallback. Normal-use final gate: BLOCKING; an incomplete security scan is reported as successful proof of absence.

4. [P2] The native Codex fallback installs to a different path from its executable link. scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:417-421 and :364. A native Codex executable without the Homebrew `codex-resources` sibling passes the native-binary check and takes the fallback tar branch, which creates `codex/codex`. The guest installer then always links `/usr/local/bin/codex` to `.../codex/bin/codex`, which does not exist in that branch; version verification fails and sandbox-up tears down. Normalize the fallback layout or select the link according to the actual layout. Normal-use final gate: NON-BLOCKING for the currently validated Atlas Homebrew cask layout; the accepted standalone-native installation path is broken and blocks Review 1.

5. [P2] The documented direct mailbox-send helper always loses its sender identity. skills/c11-computer-use/SKILL.md:64; scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:37-40, :476-479. guest_c11 explicitly removes every C11_/CMUX_ variable and supplies no guest sender identity. CLI/c11.swift:20300-20317 requires a workspace UUID in that environment and a sender tab or --from; --from alone still cannot supply the missing workspace. Therefore the documented `sandbox-agent.sh <run> c11 mailbox send --to ... --body ...` fails before writing an envelope. Either provide an explicitly selected guest sender context or replace the executable example/help with the actual guest-shell-tab send path used in validation. Normal-use final gate: NON-BLOCKING with the guest-shell-tab workaround, but the published command is unusable and blocks Review 1.

Validation: bash syntax and git diff --check passed. The probes used synthetic data and shell/scanner code in memory; no app was built/launched, no VM was started, no credential store/exporter was executed, and no secret was printed. Owner runtime evidence predates the reviewed head; this is a source review, not independent exact-head runtime proof. The approved Grok login-only exception is not a finding. No source edits, commits, pushes, or PR comments were made. Awaiting repairs in this same review session.

review r1 verify FAIL @ 1065c68e73

Delta-only verification of 97e8cc26c3..1065c68e734fb770a15276df8bf948f8d7bdc4d9 against my five Review 1 findings and the code each repair touched. Checkout is detached and clean; PR #562 was confirmed at this head. No new discovery was opened.

1. OPEN, BLOCKING [P1]: SIGINT cleanup is still incomplete. scripts/sandbox-up.sh:353-379, especially :373. The new trap handles SIGINT only if the cleanup-owning Bash process entered with a catchable SIGINT disposition. A non-interactive Bash process started asynchronously with `&` can inherit SIGINT=SIG_IGN; Bash cannot reset or trap a signal ignored at its entry. Installing this INT trap does not repair that condition. Once the background stage succeeds, wait returns 0, the traps are cleared, and sandbox-up returns success with the clone retained. This confirms a concrete code path matching the owner's reported INT result, while distinguishing it from a normal foreground cancellation.

   Independent read-only probes executed the exact repaired cleanup/staging block with fake stage/down commands: default SIGINT -> teardown, exit 1; inherited ignored SIGINT -> NO teardown, exit 0; inherited ignored SIGINT plus SIGTERM -> teardown, exit 1; stage error -> teardown, exit 1; teardown error -> explicit TEARDOWN FAILED, exit 2. No VM or app was involved.

   Required fix: establish catchable signal dispositions before the Bash process that owns provisioning/cleanup starts. For example, use a once-only exec bootstrap/supervisor that explicitly resets SIGINT (and the other cancellation signals it promises) to SIG_DFL before exec'ing the Bash worker, then retain the stage cancellation and teardown traps. Another Bash trap alone cannot undo inherited SIG_IGN. Repeat the actual Atlas launch path plus both default-disposition and inherited-ignored INT cases; cancellation must return nonzero and prove the named clone is absent. Finding 1 is not closed by the successful TERM case.

2. CLOSED: rotated credentials now fail the post-down cleanliness gate. scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:719-730, :771. Missing staged fingerprints set bad=1, which reaches the final failing verdict. The plain-variable export/fingerprint assignments also preserve command failures instead of hiding them inside array assignment. Synthetic execution of the repaired branch: unchanged fingerprint -> bad=0/exit 0; rotated fingerprint -> bad=1/exit 1. No real exporter was called.

3. CLOSED: unreadable and failed scans no longer become absence. scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:116-191, :737-743. Non-ENXIO seek/read errors, missing roots, and traversal failures propagate to exit 2; unsupported SEEK_DATA falls back to a full read; short reads fail. Probes of the actual extracted scanner: readable positive control -> found/exit 1; open denial, SEEK_DATA EIO, short read, walk denial, and missing root -> error/exit 2; SEEK_DATA EINVAL -> full-read found/exit 1. The caller treats scan errors as a failed gate. Error reporting contains paths/reasons, not matched values.

4. CLOSED: standalone Codex now uses the installer's expected layout. scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:451-458 and :393. The fallback archives Codex as codex/bin/codex, matching the executable link. Read-only tar-stream probes using a source file as the synthetic binary listed codex/bin/codex; Claude and Grok still listed claude/claude and grok/grok. Nothing was installed or executed as an agent.

5. CLOSED: the mailbox example now supplies a real guest sender path. scripts/sandbox-agent.sh:37-43, :516-519; skills/c11-computer-use/SKILL.md:64-71. Help and skill create/use a guest shell tab and send the mailbox command through that tab, where its workspace/tab environment exists. The direct helper invocation now exits with an actionable explanation instead of advertising an impossible sender-less send. The inherited host c11 environment remains stripped.

The additional repair edits (checked export/account/fingerprint assignments, revised wipe-failure wording, and research-doc explanations) introduce no regression found in this scoped pass. bash -n and git diff --check passed. This is source and isolated synthetic verification, not new Atlas runtime proof. No source edits, builds, app launches, VM starts, credential reads/exports, PR comments, commits, or pushes were performed. Reused session C11-322-Review1-1; awaiting the remaining repair.

validation r2 @ 6b5e072aafd01841816eb49c44029f00e5cc9a34 (repairs for review r1 and review r1 verify)

Heads: 1065c68e73 holds findings 1-5 plus the same-class hunt; 6b5e072aaf holds the SIGINT re-exec. All runtime proofs ran on Atlas against the Atlas worktree at the head, with `C11_SANDBOX_HOST=local`. Evidence: Atlas `~/c11-sandbox-runner/c11-322/evidence-r2*.log` and `evidence-r2/`. No secret was printed.

**1. Cancelled staging tears the clone down** (`sandbox-up.sh`). The trap is armed before staging starts; staging runs as a waited child; a failed teardown reports itself (exit 2). INT, TERM and HUP are reset to SIG_DFL by a one-time re-exec before bash runs.
- TERM during staging (r2-term): exit 1, `interrupted while staging agents; removing the clone`, `deleted=c11-sb-r2-term`, no clone left.
- Foreground Ctrl-C (pty interrupt character) during staging (r2-ctrlc): exit 1, `deleted=c11-sb-r2-ctrlc`, no clone left.
- Backgrounded launch (plain `&` under a `nohup` driver, so SIGINT was ignored on entry) sent `kill -INT` during staging (r2-bgint): exit 1, `deleted=c11-sb-r2-bgint`, no clone left. Before the re-exec, this exact case exited 0 and kept `c11-sb-r2-int` running. That clone was torn down (`deleted=c11-sb-r2-int`).
- Teardown failure (stubbed `sandbox-down` exits 1), TERM during staging (r2-downfail): exit 2, `TEARDOWN FAILED for r2-downfail. The clone may still be running with staged credentials…`. The clone was then removed with the real `sandbox-down`.
- End state: `tart list` shows no `c11-sb-r2-*` clone.

**2. Rotation fails closed** (`verify-clean`). On run r2-e2e, after a real down, `verify_clean=pass`. Adding one fingerprint to the record that no export can reproduce (`codex:0000000000000000`) gave `credentials=ROTATED: 1 of 3 staged values can no longer be exported and are not searched for … This run cannot be certified clean.` and `verify_clean=FAIL`, exit 1. With the record restored, `verify_clean=pass`.

**3. Scan errors are errors, never absence** (`secret_scan`, extracted from the script and run on synthetic files):

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| readable hit | `found`, exit 1 |
| unreadable file | `error … Permission denied`, exit 2 |
| secret behind an unreadable subdirectory (os.walk error) | `error … walk/locked (Permission denied)`, exit 2 |
| missing path | `error … No such file or directory`, exit 2 |
| SEEK_DATA EINVAL | full-read fallback, `found`, exit 1 |
| SEEK_DATA EIO | `error`, exit 2 |
| clean readable tree | `absent`, exit 0 |

In the live runs, verify-clean read 32,056,427,520 bytes of golden extents with `absent`.

**4. Codex layout matches the link.** The stage branch was run on a standalone `codex` and on a cask layout; both put the binary at `codex/bin/codex`, which is the guest link target `$lib/codex/bin/codex`.

**5. Mailbox send.** `sandbox-agent.sh r2-e2e c11 mailbox send …` now exits 1 with `mailbox send needs a sender tab. Run it in a guest shell tab: …`. The documented path (a guest shell tab from `c11 new-tab`, then `c11 send` of the `c11 mailbox send` line) delivered to lc-codex (`mailbox.accepted`, then delivered), and Codex answered `• PONG-R2`.

**Same class, hunted.** Command-substitution results inside array and associative-element assignments are now checked through a plain variable, since zsh drops the substitution's status there (export, account, fingerprints). An empty export or fingerprint dies. Wipe failure reads as a failure in `sandbox-down`. The positive control on the r2-e2e clone, `verify-clean --control`, gave `control_clone_disk=found`.

**Gates.** Atlas `remote-build.sh` at 1065c68e73: `C11_REMOTE_OK compile=ok`. 6b5e072aaf only adds the sandbox-up re-exec; its exact-head build is running and the result follows. shellcheck `-S warning` is clean on every `scripts/sandbox-*.sh`. origin/main is now f7ac4fc1ea; the branch was not rebased during review.

HANDOFF C11-322 REVIEW 6b5e072aafd01841816eb49c44029f00e5cc9a34 PR #562 + C11-322 validation r2
